A credential holding an org-level key and no workspace id sends no workspace header, so Anthropic decides what that does. The buffered and the streaming dispatch in the server call the same helper, but only the buffered one is driven by a test for dispatch (the streaming path is driven only for the invalid-stored-value refusal). Other plugins (internal_http, WASM) get the server-side removal but have no workspace-id injection of their own. The header name is matched exactly (case-insensitively); other provider headers, and the gap that /api/v1/execute does not apply a capability's model allowlist or token ceiling to a credential no LLM channel references, are not covered here (a credential an LLM channel references is refused there, see llm-credential-channel-only). The format check is an operator-facing sanity check, not Anthropic's own validation.

claims.statement: An LLM-proxy request whose model the rate card does not price is refused with 403 model_unpriced before any upstream call, because leria rejects an unpriced token event and the call would book $0 so a budget cap would never trip. With the shipped default [llm_proxy] require_priced_model = true and a rate card read from rate_card_path (the file leria reads): a model the card lacks is refused for a buffered and a streamed request and the test upstream sees no request and no meter event is written; a request with a body that names no model is refused; with no card configured every model-bearing call is refused; a priced model passes and is metered; a dated id passes only through an explicit model_ref_prefix entry, the prefix followed by - or @ and more text (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 and claude-haiku-4-5@20251001 pass, claude-haiku-4-50, the bare prefix and an id with no prefix entry do not); an entry of another asset than tokens, a zero or negative token price, an empty or malformed file and a card with no token entry are refused when the file is read; the operator opt-out require_priced_model = false lets an unpriced model through; an unreadable file is a startup error. The model that is gated, checked against the allowlist and booked is the one the resolved upstream URL selects where the URL picks it, not the body's: Gemini and Vertex AI take models/<id> (a model baked into provider_base counts; two model segments, or none outside the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, are refused), Bedrock takes the percent-decoded model/<id> (a Bedrock call with no body model passes when the path model is priced; no model segment is refused), Azure OpenAI takes deployments/<name> (or the body model as the deployment name on the v1 API) through the operator's [llm_proxy.azure_deployments] map and an unmapped deployment is refused even when its name is a priced model's id; a body model that differs from the URL's model is refused; with the URL naming an unpriced model and the body a priced one the request is refused and the upstream is not called; the capability allowlist is applied to the URL's model where the URL selects it (a Gemini, Vertex or Bedrock call whose body names no model passes an allowlist that lists the path model and is refused when it does not; an Azure call passes when the allowlist lists the mapped model or the deployment name) and to the body's model where the body picks it. A request that the proxy cannot show to bill tokens alone is refused with 403 modifier_unpriced before any upstream call, by an ALLOWLIST (default-deny), per provider protocol (anthropic-messages, openai-chat and nvidia, openai-responses, azure-openai, gemini and vertex-ai including the OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-on-Vertex bodies, bedrock-converse, bedrock-invoke; any other protocol admits no field): (1) every top-level request field must be on the protocol's table of fields that cannot change the price per token (model, messages, system, max_tokens, sampling parameters, stop sequences, stream, metadata, tools, tool_choice and the like); any other field, including compaction, context_management, fallbacks, speed, inference_geo, web_search_options, guardrailConfig and a service tier in any casing (service_tier, serviceTier, ServiceTier), is refused, and a body that is not a JSON object is refused; the card format has no entry for a priced variant, so only a code change widens a table; (2) the anthropic-beta header (every line, comma separated) and a body anthropic_beta (Bedrock InvokeModel, Vertex Anthropic) may name only betas on a priced list, any other value is refused; (3) a tool must be exactly a plain client tool of the protocol (Anthropic: an untyped or custom object with name, input_schema and no key beyond description, cache_control and strict, or an exact versioned client type bash, text_editor, memory or computer; OpenAI chat and responses: function or custom with the documented keys only; Gemini: functionDeclarations entries; Bedrock Converse: toolSpec or cachePoint with the documented keys only, in toolConfig.tools); server tools, advisor, web search and fetch, tool search, code execution, file search, grounding, urlContext, a typed tool not on the list and a tool with a foreign key are refused.; (4) inside admitted fields, the media and modality markers are an ALLOWLIST checked over the whole body, buffered and streamed, with no upstream call: for a Gemini or Vertex AI body the proxy walks every array element and every object value at any depth (a single object is read like an array, as Google's parser does, so contents, parts, systemInstruction and functionResponse parts are all reached), and an object under inlineData, inline_data, fileData or file_data is admitted only if it is an object whose mimeType or mime_type (every one present, at least one present) is a string that is image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/heic, image/heif, image/gif, application/pdf or a text/* type; a missing, non-string or any other media type (audio and video, application/octet-stream, the YouTube file_uri form with no media type) is refused; a responseModalities or response_modalities at any depth must be a non-empty array of exactly TEXT entries (an empty array, a non-array and any other entry are refused; an absent field and a JSON null are admitted); a JSON null under inlineData, inline_data, fileData or file_data is read like an absent key; a body nested deeper than 64 levels is refused; for an OpenAI chat, responses or Azure body each messages or input entry (an array or a single object) and each content part (an array or a single object) must be of type text, image_url, input_text, input_image, output_text or refusal (an entry may also be a plain string, or of a conversation item type message, function_call, function_call_output, custom_tool_call, custom_tool_call_output, reasoning or item_reference; an entry with no type is admitted and only its content parts are checked), a message carrying an audio object is refused (an audio of null is read like an absent key), and an image_url part (a string or an object with url) or an input_image part whose URL starts with data: (any casing) is admitted only when the media type between data: and the first ; or , (trimmed, lowercased) is one of the priced types above, so a data:audio/wav, data:video/mp4 or typeless data: URL is refused on every OpenAI dialect, including the Gemini and Vertex AI OpenAI-compatible chat route, while an https URL is admitted (input_audio, file and input_file parts, a PDF included, a part with no type and any other type are refused, so a PDF part passes only on Gemini; an audio output request, the modalities and audio fields, is refused by the top-level table); a plain text request, image parts, a Gemini PDF part, TEXT-only modalities and a request with no modalities field pass. Other nested options are not inspected. A plain priced request passes. GET /api/v1/posture reports rate_card.require_priced_model, configured, entries, last_error, sha256 (of the card read at start, the digest leria reports for the same file), file_sha256 (the file as last read) and never the path.

claims.does_not_establish: Only the /llm proxy is gated: a model call through POST /api/v1/execute, an MCP http.request or a named tool is not refused here (leria still rejects its unpriced token event and books $0). The model is the one the upstream URL or the body names; it does not show which model the provider bills if it serves a different one (the token event then carries the served id, see llm-token-event-complete-and-priced). Azure deployment names are mapped to models by the operator, and a wrong map entry prices the wrong model. The allowlist is checked on top-level field names and on tool and beta values; the contents of an allowed field (for example generationConfig, thinking, response_format, inferenceConfig, metadata) are not inspected, except the media and modality markers named in the statement (any other nested option is not inspected). The media allowlist assumes that image, PDF and text input bill at the model's token rate, because the rate card holds one input and one output price per model: a provider that prices image or document input differently is booked at the base price (an under-count) until that type is removed from the list. A request with no responseModalities is admitted, and the default output modality of a model is priced only through that model's card entry. The proxy checks the DECLARED media type (the mimeType or mime_type of a Gemini part, or the type written in a data: URL): the inline bytes are not inspected, and a URL the provider fetches (http or https, gs://, a Files API reference, a YouTube fileUri) is not inspected, so a media type that disagrees with the bytes or a fetched file of an unpriced type is not caught. The output arrays of function_call_output and custom_tool_call_output items are not scanned for content parts. The walk reads keys by name anywhere in a Gemini body, so a tool argument that happens to use one of those key names is refused too (fail closed); the OpenAI check reads only the messages and input entries and their content parts, and an OpenAI item type outside the list (a server tool call replayed as input, for example) is refused until priced, so a provider that prices a nested option is booked at the base price (an under-count) until its table entry is reviewed; a field on a table is a human pricing judgment, not a proof. The OpenAI-Beta header and the other forwarded provider headers are not on a beta allowlist. The regional-endpoint premium of a Vertex or Bedrock deployment reached through provider_base and a price the provider changes without a request field are booked at the base price. The card is read for coverage only: prices are not checked beyond being positive, the file is not compared with the copy leria loaded (the posture fingerprint is what a deploy check compares), a change is noticed by size and modified time, and a file edited back to the same size within the filesystem's timestamp granularity is not re-read. Staleness of a card is not enforced. What happens when the file changes after start is rate-card-reload-only-narrows. The upstream is a test double, not a live provider.

claims.statement: A metered LLM call is charged for all billed input and output that the top-level usage block reports, and under a model the rate card prices. Every entry of usage.iterations (one per sampling step, including server-side compaction and advisor steps that the top-level counts leave out) is counted: per direction the booked count is the larger of the top-level figure and the sum over the iterations (each entry's cache tokens included, cache writes at twice), so no step is counted twice and none is left out, for a buffered response and for a stream (the largest cumulative list wins; an estimate keeps it as a floor). A request that runs features the card does not price is refused before the upstream (unpriced-model-refused). Anthropic cache_creation_input_tokens (Bedrock cacheWriteInputTokens) are added to the input count at TWICE the input price, an upper bound for both cache lifetimes (the provider bills 1.25x and 2x), and cache_read_input_tokens (cacheReadInputTokens) at the full input price: for a buffered response with usage input 10, cache creation 100, cache read 1000 the token event carries input_tokens 1210; the same for an Anthropic stream, where the cache counts of message_start are added once (a cumulative repeat in message_delta is not summed again) and an estimate keeps the cache tokens it saw; OpenAI prompt_tokens, which already includes cached tokens, is not changed, and a huge cache count saturates instead of wrapping. Gemini usageMetadata books promptTokenCount plus toolUsePromptTokenCount as input and candidatesTokenCount plus thoughtsTokenCount as output (streamed: the largest cumulative value of each, never summed twice, and the thinking tokens are a floor of an estimate), and a block with a prompt count and no candidates (a blocked response) still books its prompt. With a rate card configured the token event's dims.model_ref is the model the provider served when the card prices it; the requested model (the one the gate checked, which for Gemini, Vertex, Bedrock and Azure is the one the URL selects) is used only when the served id is a dated form of it (the requested id followed by - or @ and more text) and the card prices the requested one; any other served model, priced or not, is booked under its own id, so a served Opus is never booked at a requested Haiku's price. This holds for buffered and streamed calls. With no card, or with neither covered, it is the served model, then the requested one.

claims.does_not_establish: The cache tokens are booked as input tokens because the card has one input price per model: a cache read is OVER-counted (the provider bills about 0.1x) and a cache write is never under-counted but is over-counted for the 5-minute cache (1.25x billed, 2x booked); it does not model provider cache pricing and does not read cache_creation.ephemeral_* to split the lifetimes. Only the Anthropic, Bedrock and Gemini spellings are read, and a provider that reports cache tokens or reasoning tokens elsewhere (OpenAI reasoning inside completion_tokens is already counted by the provider) is not counted beyond what its usage block reports. Server-tool fees and price modifiers are not metered (the proxy refuses every request field, beta and tool off its allowlist, see unpriced-model-refused). usage.iterations entries are charged at the request model's input and output price whatever model an entry names (an advisor step on a dearer model is under-priced, which is why the advisor tool stays refused); only the Anthropic and Bedrock spellings of the list are read. A served model the card does not price is booked under its own id and leria then rejects the event as unpriced and holds its watermark; the gate is what prevents that on /llm for the model the request names, not for a provider that substitutes a different one. The upstream is a test double, not a live provider. Says nothing about leria pricing the event.

claims.statement: The rate card read at start bounds what vultrino covers for the life of the process, and the file parses as strictly as leria's. After start a changed card file is re-read, and the covered set is the intersection of the start card and the latest good file: a model added to the file stays refused (leria loaded the start card and could not price it), a model removed is refused at once, the start coverage returns when the file returns to the start content, and a change that cannot be parsed keeps the previous card and is reported as last_error. The posture sha256 stays the start card's fingerprint and file_sha256 reports the file as last read. The parser refuses what leria's refuses: an unknown field on a card or an entry (a typo such as output_price_micros_per_unti), a missing, empty or repeated rate_card_version, an input or output price given on one side only, an entry with no price in a symmetric card, a non-token entry in a card that uses the input/output form or a prefix, a duplicate entry and a created_at that is not RFC3339; the optional provider, created_at and stale_after_s fields are accepted.
claims.does_not_establish: That the two planes read the same bytes at start: the deploy mounts one file and verify-posture compares the sha256 values, vultrino does not compare them itself. A leria restart onto a newer file is matched here only by a vultrino restart. Rust parsing is stricter than leria's in places (field names are case-sensitive here, a duplicate entry is refused in every card form), so a file leria accepts may be refused here; the reverse is what the claim is about. Prices are not read beyond being positive. A change is noticed by size and modified time. The test files are temporary files in one process, not a mounted ConfigMap.

claims.statement: vultrino vault backup copies the vault snapshot, its .wal, the outbox and the averin stores while holding the exclusive vault lock (released before the password open check, which runs the KDF on the copy), into a new empty directory, with a manifest of SHA-256 sums and sizes; it refuses a vault that has no .wal (a partial backup), a destination that is not empty, and checks the copy by re-reading it against the manifest and by opening it under the password. vultrino vault restore checks the manifest, every checksum and size, and that nothing is in the directory that the manifest does not list, requires the snapshot and the .wal in the manifest, and opens the copy, all before it touches the target; it refuses to replace an existing vault without --force (then moves the old files aside, never deletes them), stages every file before renaming any (the averin queue as a whole sibling directory, renamed into place after the old one is moved aside, so a target that already has a queue restores cleanly), accepts only manifest names a backup can contain (never an arbitrary name written into the vault directory), and while it runs leaves <vault>.restore-pending, which makes FileStorage refuse to open until the restore is re-run. A restored vault holds the kill that was in its .wal. vault backup also refuses while <vault>.restore-pending exists, so a half-applied restore is never copied into a 'verified' backup.
claims.does_not_establish: Rollback to an older but self-consistent backup, or a backup tampered with together with its manifest by someone who can write the backup directory: the manifest is not signed. A backup taken while a process holds the vault or the durable averin queue is refused after 30 seconds (vault) or at once (queue), not tested with a second OS process. Power-loss durability of the restore renames: a crash between them is covered by the marker, which is tested only by presence, not by injecting a crash. The averin queue segments are copied as files and are not opened by the open check. Backups of a vault on a filesystem without flock semantics. Both commands expect the service to be stopped: a running non-durable service holds the vault lock only per operation, so restore does not detect it. Any CI run. Restoring an older backup undoes every kill, revocation and approval made after it; the operator must re-apply them (documented, not detected).

claims.statement: vultrino vault check opens the snapshot and a copy of the .wal in a scratch directory. A vault that opens is reported healthy. A vault that does not open is reported as having a damaged final record only when removing exactly the last complete .wal line makes it open; then, only with --truncate-final, that line is written to <wal>.damaged-<nanos> and cut from the .wal. Damage in a middle line, or a wrong password, makes the vault fail to open even without the final line, so the command refuses and the .wal is unchanged.
claims.does_not_establish: That the cut record was unimportant: it is a committed mutation (possibly a kill or a revocation) and is lost, so the operator must redo it; the command prints that and keeps the removed bytes. Damage in the snapshot, in a middle record, or a torn tail beyond the final record (a torn tail is already ignored at open). Concurrent use: it takes the exclusive locks and expects the service to be stopped. One damaged final line only; two damaged final lines need the command run twice and are refused if the first cut does not make the vault open. Any CI run.

claims.statement: With [averin] enabled, mode observe and d8_complete_evidence on (the FeirOS Solo posture), on both the buffered and the streaming tail, the action classes refused before the plugin runs when Averin cannot begin the two-phase use evidence depend on the operator setting [averin] d8_evidence_floor. In both modes an action with no catalog declaration is refused with the error D8 before-act evidence failed, and a declared-irreversible action never runs or degrades. Money is an action in the money.* namespace or one the catalog declares irreversible. Default money_and_irreversible: money actions are refused, including a partially-reversible one such as money.notify, while a partially-reversible non-money action and a declared-Reversible action whose evidence cannot be begun because Averin is unavailable (unreachable, 5xx or 429) still run, with one use receipt sealed through the mode's own rule, an AVERIN-D8-DEGRADED alarm line and a d8_degraded counter increment. human_floor: every partially-reversible action is refused as well, and only a declared-Reversible action still degrades. A declared non-reversible action is human-floor for approval: on the direct path it is sent to approval (the error says approval is required) and never runs or degrades before approval, and the D8 before-act evidence refusal and the degrade of a partially-reversible action are shown on the approved buffered resume only, not on the streaming tail. A declared-Reversible action is refused, not degraded, when a live Averin answers 4xx, and when its params exceed max_seal_params_bytes (refused before the use token is spent). The default floor is only in force with a live Averin client (averin enabled, base_url and resource_id set, no plain http to a public host) and d8_complete_evidence on; with no client there is no evidence path, so a partially-reversible action is refused rather than run with no seal, and the posture reports human_floor. A reversible-class action named money.* is refused, never degraded. With d8_complete_evidence off the setting has no effect and every non-reversible approved action keeps its committed-evidence requirement. An unknown d8_evidence_floor value is refused at config load, the default parses to money_and_irreversible, and the running mode is reported in the posture. With Averin up, a reversible action gets use-intent before and use-outcome after the call and no degraded count.
claims.detector: cargo test --locked --no-default-features --test approval_token_integration -- --exact solo_posture_with_averin_down_refuses_irreversible_and_runs_reversible solo_posture_with_averin_up_gives_reversible_two_phase_evidence irreversible_approval_resume_refuses_failed_seal_even_in_observe_mode reversible_approval_resume_remains_fail_open_when_observe_seal_is_missing default_floor_degrades_a_partially_reversible_write_but_refuses_money_and_irreversible default_floor_refuses_a_partially_reversible_write_when_no_averin_client_exists human_floor_mode_refuses_every_partially_reversible_action floor_setting_has_no_effect_without_d8_complete_evidence && cargo test --locked --no-default-features --test d8_degraded_guard && cargo test --locked --no-default-features --test solo_evidence_posture
claims.does_not_establish: Only an action the trusted catalog declares Reversible or partially-reversible may degrade, and in the default mode only when it is not money; whether an operator declared the real side effect truthfully, or named a money action under money.*, is not checked, and a reversible catalog entry named money.* requested under another label is not recognised as money. Unavailable means a request error (connect or timeout), a 5xx or a 429; a live Averin that misbehaves in some other way refuses, which is the safe side. In the default mode a degraded partially-reversible write has no before-act record. The approved-resume path (including every partially-reversible case) is driven through the buffered tail in approval_token_integration and the direct path through both tails in d8_degraded_guard; the D8 evidence refusal of a declared non-reversible action on the streaming tail is not driven by any test; a fake Averin stands in for the real one, and the four-plane evidence-gate end-to-end is a separate run. The routine action's one-phase seal can still be lost: the plan 085 reconciliation detects the gap, it cannot recover it. An approval opened under an older build for a partially-reversible action is refused on resume. Any CI run other than the recorded one.

claims.statement: With [averin] enabled in Observe mode, every use receipt that does not reach Averin is recorded as an individual gap, not only counted: a failed or timed-out async seal, a seal dropped because the async fan-out was saturated, params over max_seal_params_bytes (async and durable paths), a failed local durable enqueue, a durable use receipt that exhausted its delivery attempts (a dead-lettered grant is not a receipt and records none), and a seal task lost before it recorded an outcome; each gap carries the token id, project, request id, use sequence number, one of six fixed reasons and a detail clipped to 200 characters, and never the params; the pending buffer holds at most 4096 gaps and a gap that does not fit is counted in receipt_gaps_overflowed; gaps returned for retry go back to the front in their original order; and flush_receipt_gaps_once appends each pending gap to the signed outbox as one evidence.receipt_gap event whose subject is the use token id, so the oldest gap is the first appended and a second flush appends nothing. The action itself is never blocked or failed by any of this. An [averin] block with enabled = true and an empty resource_id, or a base_url that is empty, does not parse or is plain http:// to a public address, does not load (config error naming the field and that no receipt would be recorded), and VultrinoServer::try_new refuses to start when the seal client still cannot be built, so Observe cannot run silently without a seal client; a disabled block is not judged.
claims.does_not_establish: Gaps are held in memory and appended to the outbox every two seconds: a process that is killed before an append loses the gaps it had not yet written, and the counters with them. flush_receipt_gaps_once puts a gap back for retry when an outbox append fails, but no test makes an append fail, so that branch is not exercised here (the requeue order is). A gap says an action ran without a receipt; it does not say the action's own side effect succeeded, and it is not a proof that no other receipt is missing: a seal that Averin accepted but recorded wrongly, a seal that never started because Averin is disabled, undeclared actions, and receipts lost to a crash between the action and the seal enqueue are outside it. The on_execute (synchronous) Observe arms record gaps by the same call but are not exercised by a test here; only the production async and durable paths are. The outbox event reaches a consumer only if one polls or is pushed to; nothing here shows that anything alerts on it. The vacuity of the name filter: the detector selects tests whose name contains fei33_, so a renamed test drops out of it. The refusal covers a client that cannot be built: a block that builds but names an unreachable averin, or an AVERIN_API_KEY averin rejects, still starts, and every Observe action is then recorded as a receipt gap rather than refused. The gap is an outbox event, and the outbox prunes every event older than [outbox] retention_secs (2 days by default) whether or not it was delivered, so this claim does not keep a gap past that window: keeping it is the consumer's job (govder stores each gap before acknowledging the push, govder claim receipt-gap-durable-record), and a consumer that is down or unconfigured for longer than the window loses the gaps in it. The plain-http check resolves a host name when the config loads; a name that resolves to a public address only later is caught by the connect-time guard, not by the load refusal. The binary's three server constructions use try_new; the library's VultrinoServer::new panics instead of returning the error.

claims.statement: With [approvals.telegram] callback_decisions = true, the Telegram notifier posts callback buttons carrying only the approval id (no decision link or token is in the message), and a button press is decided as the person Telegram reports: a user listed in [approvals.telegram.approvers] is recorded under their mapped identity with channel telegram:<user id>, so two different users are two approvers and complete a dual-control request only together, and the same user pressing twice is one approver; a user who is not listed, a press from outside the configured chat, data that is not this module's, an unknown approval and an approval that is already decided each record nothing and answer the presser; config load refuses a non-numeric chat id, an empty approvers table, two Telegram users mapped to one identity (compared case-insensitively), a user listed twice, a non-positive or non-numeric user id, a blank identity, an identity with the reserved verified: or agg: prefix, and an approvers table without callback_decisions = true; and the default URL buttons are unchanged, whose decision-link route records the single oob_approver_identity, so two link clicks never complete a two-person action while one link click plus one sign-off under another identity does (a link verdict is one approver of unknown identity, possibly the same person as the other sign-off); and a Telegram identity collides with a verified panel sign-off only when the mapped string equals the IdP subject (unit tests fei16_a_link_is_one_unknown_identity... and fei16_telegram_and_panel_dedupe...).
claims.detector: cargo test --locked --no-default-features --lib -- approval::telegram_callbacks:: config::types::tests::fei16_ approval::tests::fei16_ && cargo test --locked --no-default-features --test web_smoke -- fei16_decision_links_cannot_complete_a_two_person_action
claims.does_not_establish: The identity is the operator's mapping from a Telegram user id, taken from callback_query.from.id as Telegram's servers report it; the tests use a stand-in Telegram server, so they do not show what the real API sends, that its user ids are unforgeable in a chat (that is Telegram's property, not checked here), or that a Telegram account is held by the person the mapping names (a stolen or shared account is that person). A press carries no approver class, so an approval gated by a govder recipe that names classes cannot be satisfied this way; the tests do not run such a recipe. A bot can have one getUpdates consumer and a webhook disables polling: a second consumer or a set webhook makes the loop retry with backoff and log, and no test shows that. Only the web process starts the poll loop. The mapping to the IdP subject is an operator duty that nothing checks: a Telegram user mapped to an email is counted as a different person from the same human's verified panel sign-off. The webhook notifier's links are unchanged and still unattributed; the tests cover only the Telegram link route's behaviour for a two-person request. The callback path records the decision and resumes the action through the same functions as the link and panel paths, but the resume itself is not exercised here.

claims.statement: The secret-alignment fingerprint is the first 16 bytes (32 lowercase hex characters) of HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the secret over `feir-secret-alignment/v1:` followed by the relationship name, reproduces every vector of vectors/secret-fingerprint.v1.json (generated by an independent Python reference, owned by feir-os), is different for two relationships under one secret, and does not exist for an empty secret; and GET /api/v1/posture reports, per relationship, the fingerprints of the values vultrino is configured with: vultrino-outbox-poll (the [outbox] hmac_secret), vultrino-approval-push (the same secret, only while push delivery is enabled and has a URL), workload-assertion (one fingerprint per verifier secret the workload exchange accepts, the same comma-separated list it verifies with, so a rotation overlap reports both, and only while the exchange is configured and valid), tenant-assertion (the secret it signs calls to govder with), averin-api-key (the AVERIN_API_KEY it sends to averin, only while the [averin] seal client is enabled, with the posture averin.api_key_configured flag true under the same condition, which feir-os's averin_use_checks reads) and approver-key (the key that verifies the broker's approver decisions, absent when that key is unset, equal to the shared key or blank), omits a relationship whose secret is unset, and carries no secret value in the body.
claims.detector: cargo test --locked --no-default-features --lib -- secret_fp::tests web::posture::tests::report_carries_a_fingerprint_per_relationship_and_no_secret web::posture::tests::report_omits_the_push_relationship_when_the_outbox_does_not_push web::posture::tests::report_omits_unset_secrets_and_an_unusable_approver_key web::posture::tests::report_carries_the_averin_key_fingerprint_only_while_the_seal_client_is_on web::posture::tests::report_carries_averin_api_key_configured_with_the_fingerprint_condition web::posture::tests::report_carries_a_workload_assertion_fingerprint_per_verifier_secret && cargo test --locked --no-default-features --test workload_exchange_integration -- --exact posture_reports_exactly_the_secrets_the_exchange_verifies_with && cargo test --locked --no-default-features --test posture_averin_report
claims.does_not_establish: That two planes hold the same value: this is the report one plane makes, and the comparison is feir-os's verifier. The report reads the loaded configuration, so a value changed afterwards or read by another code path is not reflected; a vultrino whose outbox pushes somewhere other than govder still reports the push relationship, which the verifier then compares with govder's GOVDER_SIGNATURE_SECRET. The fingerprint is only as private as the secret is strong: someone who holds it can test guesses for a low-entropy secret offline, and the report is protected only by a global admin key. The route's key gate is covered by the posture-report claims, not here. The cross-plane check that real binaries emit what the verifier reads is govder's armed four-plane e2e (TestFourPlanePostureE2E, TestFourPlaneSecretMismatchE2E). The averin-api-key fingerprint says which key vultrino sends; that averin accepts it is checked by feir-os's verifier against averin's own report, and no four-plane run has a keyed averin. The workload-assertion fingerprints say which verifier secrets vultrino accepts; that feir-runtime-edge holds one of them is the feir-os verifier's comparison, and no run here starts a real feir-runtime-edge against a real vultrino and feeds both reports to evaluate.jq (the integration test signs with the listed secrets itself).

claims.statement: A credential referenced by an LLM-proxy capability (llm configured on a stored capability) is usable only through the /llm proxy. The match is on credential identity: each such capability's credential_ref is resolved through the same resolver execution uses and compared by credential id with the credential being used, so a capability that names the credential by its vault id and a request that names it by alias (or the reverse) are both refused; the spelling comparison is kept as well. POST /api/v1/execute answers 403 llm_credential_channel_only and the MCP http_request tool returns the same refusal as a tool error, in both cases after the use-token scope and tenant-isolation checks (a cross-tenant or out-of-scope attempt keeps its own error and detect event) and before policy evaluation, approval, use-token consumption, evidence or any upstream call: the upstream plugin is never invoked, no meter event is emitted and a one-use token keeps its use count of 0. A credential no LLM-proxy capability references still works through execute and http_request, and the /llm proxy (buffered and streaming) still works, because it alone calls the crate-private channel entries. A capability catalog that cannot be read, or a credential_ref lookup that fails for a reason other than the credential not existing, refuses the request instead of admitting it. An approval on an LLM credential is never resumed: resume refuses it terminally, because the approval record does not say which channel opened it.
claims.detector: set -e; cargo test --locked --no-default-features --test llm_proxy_integration llm_credential; cargo test --locked --no-default-features --test llm_proxy_integration non_llm_credential; cargo test --locked --no-default-features --test approval_token_integration llm_credential
claims.does_not_establish: That the unreadable-catalog refusal is exercised (no test injects a storage failure; the branch is a plain early return). That a provider key stored a second time as a credential that no LLM-proxy capability references is refused: it is an ordinary credential governed only by its policies. That the MCP named-tool path is driven by its own test for this refusal: named tools reach the same prepare_execution check, but only execute and http_request are driven here. Resume is driven only for an approval opened before the credential backed an LLM channel; a /llm-opened approval is refused by the same unconditional check but is not separately driven. A capability whose credential_ref names no existing credential is matched by spelling only. The resolver is read once per LLM capability per generic dispatch; a credential created or renamed after the catalog read is judged by the state at that read. One extra catalog read per generic dispatch is the cost. Model, price and token limits on /llm itself are covered by their own tests, not this claim.
